transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-31 16:00 UTC — Duration 52 mins; Recording: enabled; Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Elmwood CTO), Priya Kapoor (Elmwood Lead ML Engineer), Marcus Li (Elmwood SRE), Rhea Mathews (Elmwood Product)

Auto-summary (auto): Elmwood evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for a conversational routing product with strict p95 latency goals (150ms for short responses, 400ms for longer streaming). Primary concerns: concurrent sessions, streaming token/sec, prefix/KV caching, encryption/KMS, and predictable cost modeling. Agreed next steps: benchmark plan, security docs, and lab POC.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for doing this — I know we're all juggling — quick intros, I'll kick off. I'm Alex, I'll be your AE, Samira is our systems SE who will run the bench stuff.
00:18 Jordan (Elmwood CTO): Thanks Alex. Jordan here, CTO. Priya is our ML lead, Marcus runs infra, Rhea is PM. We're trying to decide hosting mode — we have latency SLOs, we care about cost, and we have some data residency needs.
00:33 Samira (Redwood SE): Great; real quick, can you sketch the workload? bursty vs steady, average tokens per convo, streaming use?
00:45 Priya (Elmwood): Mostly chat flows — about 60% short queries (10–50 tokens in reply), 40% longer streaming responses (200–800 tokens). Peak concurrency around 1.2k concurrent sessions in north-america, global tails add another ~200. We occasionally see token-surges during promos.
01:07 Marcus (Elmwood): Our p95 goal is ~150ms for short responses, and for streaming we want initial token within 300–400ms and stable token/sec afterwards. If that's not possible, we need predictable tail behavior.
01:25 Alex: Okay that's really helpful. A few quick clarifying q's — are you sensitive to cold starts? Any requirement for on-prem or can you use VPC/private plane?
01:35 Jordan: Cold starts are okay once a day, but we can't have sustained slowdowns during a sale. We are open to private deployments for regulated customers but would like Redwood hosted for simple use-cases if it meets p95.
01:52 Samira: Noted. Two main axes we'll look at: latency (p95) and throughput (tokens/sec and concurrency). We'll propose three profiles: hosted default, dedicated reserved GPU pools, and private (VPC/on-prem). Each has tradeoffs on cost and isolation.
02:10 Priya: Can you explain the prefix/KV cache thing? We've heard Redwood has automatic caching — how does that affect p95?
02:22 Samira: Sure — we do prefix and KV caching. For conversational flows, prefix caching can serve repeated system or prompt prefixes without reprocessing the entire context which reduces tokens and compute for short answers. KV cache reduces re-attending to previous tokens when continuing streams. In practice for your mix, caching can cut p95 significantly for short replies — sometimes by 30–60%, depending on prompt variability.
02:51 Jordan: Interesting. How about quantization? We are evaluating int8 models to save cost — will that affect latency or quality?
03:00 Samira: Quantization lowers memory and can improve throughput on some hardware but may add a few ms to per-token compute on others; quality impact depends on model. We recommend experiment with 8-bit for high-volume steady calls. Redwood Optimize will suggest model/quantization per workload.
03:18 Marcus: On infra — during bursts we need a predictable fallback. Does Redwood do automatic fallback to cheaper models or other regions?
03:26 Alex: Yes, we can set routing policies: region, latency, cost tiers. You can set automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to a dedicated pool. For strict SLOs we usually do canary allocs and a warm standby.
03:40 Rhea: Are there examples of customers hitting p95 under 200ms for short replies on hosted?
03:46 Samira: We have a couple — situational, depends on prompt length, seq length, and whether streaming is enabled. We have internal benchmarks; I'll share a short-hosted baseline for similar conversational patterns.
03:58 Priya: Cool. For the benchmark plan, we can provide a replay of production traffic — will you accept anonymized prompts?
04:05 Samira: Absolutely — anonymized is best. Also, we recommend a two-phase bench: first synthetic steady-state to measure throughput, then a burst simulation to exercise autoscaling and fallback.
04:20 Alex: Quick note — what's your current model stack? self-hosting open models, or third-party APIs?
04:26 Jordan: We run a mix — internal tuned open models (Llama variants) in staging, but product uses OpenAI for some features. We're trying to reduce dependence on third-party and make costs predictable.
04:34 Samira: Got it — that influences the hosting decision. If you want private deployment we can run your tuned model in a VPC package; otherwise we can serve a compatible Redwood-verified model in hosted.
04:47 Marcus: Question on encryption/KMS: for private we need HSM-backed key management and audit logs. Is that supported?
04:53 Alex: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logging. Dedicated has audit logs as well; hosted has standard encryption at rest/ in transit and can meet SOC2 needs with additional contractual terms.
05:04 Jordan: Good. Cost tradeoffs — can we get a quick back-of-envelope now for hosted vs dedicated?
05:10 Alex: Very rough: hosted per-token for your workload might be cheaper at low concurrency but dedicated reserved capacity gives a lower per-token when you're at steady 1k+ concurrency due to amortized GPU usage; private has higher upfront infra cost but gives control and potential lower marginal cost. We'll run scenarios in the benchmark plan.
05:29 Priya: On streaming — does Redwood stream token-by-token or chunked? We care about first-token latency and steady-state tokens/sec.
05:37 Samira: We support streaming token-by-token and configurable chunking. For steady-state throughput we measure tokens/sec and also track jitter. We'll instrument p95 for first-token, p95 for token-lattice (inter-token latency) and average tokens/sec.
05:53 Jordan: Could you outline what metrics you will capture in the POC bench?
05:58 Samira: Sure. We'll capture: first-token p50/p95/p99, tail latency per token, tokens/sec sustained, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, memory/kv growth, and request queueing/backpressure. We'll also capture cost-per-token and projected monthly spend per scenario.
06:20 Marcus: What about multiplexing and batching—if we set a tight latency SLO will batching hurt us?
06:28 Samira: There's always a tradeoff. Continuous batching and adaptive time windows let us increase throughput without sacrificing p95 too much. For ultra-low p95 you can set tighter batching max-wait times; Redwood Optimize suggests batching thresholds by workload.
06:45 Rhea: Any limitations for web-socket streaming across mobile clients?
06:50 Alex: No special limitations — streaming over websockets is supported; issues are usually network jitter and client-side buffering. We instrument end-to-end to help with SLO attribution.
07:01 Priya: Let's talk numbers — if our target is 150ms p95 for 30–50 token replies, what hardware and hosting do you recommend?
07:10 Samira: For that p95 you typically need high-frequency GPUs or optimized tensor cores and short sequence optimization. On hosted, we have tuned instances that can reach this on smaller models with good caching. Dedicated with reserved A100-like class or H100 and our runtime kernel selection gives you most headroom. Private can match it but depends on your infra specs.
07:35 Jordan: Do you have a recommended target tokens/sec per GPU for our mix?
07:39 Samira: Rough ballpark: for small models with quantization, you might see 1.2–2M tokens/sec per GPU under steady multiplexing; larger models will be lower. But that number is sensitive to prompt length distribution and streaming overhead. We'll profile with your prompts.
07:58 Marcus: Suppose we want an SLO of 150ms p95 — what concurrency per GPU is realistic?
08:04 Samira: It depends on model and batching; typically for a small optimized model you might target 80–200 concurrent sessions per GPU for tight p95; for larger models you might be in the single digits. We'll dimension in the bench.
08:19 Jordan: Ok. On failover — if a region hits capacity what is the customer-visible impact?
08:25 Alex: You can configure graceful degradation: route to a lower-cost model, increase batching tolerances, or fallback to a dedicated pool. We recommend canarying the fallback so you can observe quality impact.
08:38 Priya: Any stopgaps for prompt-level regression detection during rollouts?
08:43 Samira: We integrate evals tied to prompt sets; if quality drops on key prompts you can auto-roll back. We can wire your prod prompt set into the eval pipeline.
08:54 Jordan: Great. Now, for the bench, can you include a streaming-specific test that measures initial token latency and tokens/sec over 60s sustained?
09:00 Samira: Yes — we'll include a 60s sustained streaming test and a burst pattern (10x traffic for 60s).
09:07 Marcus: How long to provision a dedicated pool for testing?
09:10 Alex: We can provision a dedicated dev pool in ~48–72 hours depending on capacity. Private POC usually takes longer due to networking (a week to two).
09:20 Rhea: Security/compliance — do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC?
09:24 Alex: Yes, SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC role mapping — supported across dedicated and private. Hosted supports enterprise SSO and audit trails as well.
09:33 Priya: Any gotchas with stateful session KV caching and GDPR/data residency?
09:38 Samira: For cached state we can set eviction and residency controls; Private gives the most control for residency. If you need EU-only tokens and caching, we'd recommend a Private or Dedicated region-specific pool.
09:51 Jordan: Competitors — we've seen Anthropic and MosaicML claims on latency — how do you compare?
09:57 Alex: Competitors vary; we emphasize production operational controls (routing, cache, fallback). We'll provide benchmark methodology rather than point claims. Samira can run a direct bench if you want a 1:1 comparison.
10:10 Priya: Let's walk through a sample benchmark flow now — break it down.
10:16 Samira: Phase 1: baseline hosted with synthetic mix to measure first-token p95 and tokens/sec. Phase 2: replay your anonymized traffic. Phase 3: burst and failover tests across hosting modes. We'll produce a results dashboard with per-model and per-hosting breakdown.
10:33 Marcus: For replay, do you need the entire conversation context or just the user prompts?
10:37 Samira: Both ideally — context affects sequence length and KV hits. If you can't provide full context, provide enough preceding tokens to approximate.
10:46 Jordan: Licensing/legal — any data retention in hosted?
10:50 Alex: Hosted can be configured for shorter retention; dedicated and private give you more retention control. We'll share the security whitepaper and retention options.
10:58 Priya: On monitoring — does Redwood give token-level cost breakdowns?
11:02 Samira: Yes — cost by token, by route, by model, and token type. Console shows per-route latency breakdowns.
11:11 Rhea: OK — what would success look like for this POC?
11:14 Jordan: For us: p95 under 150ms on short replies, predictable tokens/sec during bursts without >10% error rate, and a clear cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Also security signoff for regulated accounts.
11:29 Alex: Perfect — we can hit those. I'll send the benchmark plan and estimate. Samira will own the bench execution.
11:36 Samira: We'll also include a streaming SLO playbook for how to tune batching and cache.
11:41 Jordan: Any risk points we should call out now?
11:44 Samira: The main risks are prompt variability diluting cache hits, and model quality regression when switching quantized models — we'll instrument both. Also networking jitter for mobile clients.
11:57 Marcus: Last quick: can we do a single-day in-lab with Redwood for private POC?
12:02 Alex: Yes, we can arrange an in-lab day once you sign the POC agreement; we'll run an intensive benchmark and hand over artifacts.
12:09 Jordan: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
12:12 Alex: Recap: Alex send bench plan + pricing; Samira send streaming SLO doc and bench scripts; Jordan provide anonymized prompts and peak telemetry; schedule lab for week of 2027-09-13.
12:24 Rhea: I'll coordinate internally on scheduling and legal intake.
12:27 Alex: Great — any other questions?
12:30 Priya: No, thanks all. Looking forward.
12:32 Jordan: Thanks.

End of meeting.
